claim: Structural uncertainty signals (across-trial ranking instability and within-trial candidate ambiguity) provide information complementary to answer dispersion for identifying unreliable reasoning instances on logical and mathematical reasoning tasks, but on factual retrieval tasks the structural signal collapses toward uniformity, making it uninformative.
falsifier: On a held-out set of logical reasoning tasks, the combined structural+dispersion estimator should yield higher Sel-AUC than dispersion alone; on a held-out set of factual retrieval tasks, the structural component should show near-zero correlation with accuracy and fail to improve Sel-AUC.

exclusions: limited to the five LLMs and eight benchmarks studied; transfer beyond these systems and tasks is unestablished
